cimoliopterus:enwiki:4.title: Cimoliopterus (Discovery of more complete relatives and resulting interpretations)

facts.statement: The genus Cimoliopterus was described by Rodrigues and Kellner in 2013.
facts.quote: authority: Rodrigues & Kellner, 2013

facts.statement: Fossils of Cimoliopterus date to the Cenomanian stage.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Cenomanian~

facts.statement: Cimoliopterus lived during the Late Cretaceous in what is now England and the United States.
facts.quote: Cimoliopterus is a genus of pterosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous in what is now England and the United States.

facts.statement: In 2019, Cimoliopterus was classified within the family Cimoliopteridae and the clade Targaryendraconia.
facts.quote: Cimoliopterus was moved to the family Cimoliopteridae within the clade Targaryendraconia in 2019

facts.statement: Camposipterus is considered the closest relative of Cimoliopterus.
facts.quote: with its closest relative being Camposipterus

facts.statement: Cimoliopterus can be distinguished from related pterosaurs by having a premaxillary crest that begins further back on the snout.
facts.quote: Cimoliopterus can be distinguished from related pterosaurs in features such as having a premaxillary crest that begins hindward on the snout

facts.statement: Cimoliopterus would have been covered in pycnofibres and had extensive wing-membranes supported by long wing-fingers.
facts.quote: As pterosaurs, Cimoliopterus would have been covered in pycnofibres (hair-like filaments), and had extensive wing-membranes, which were distended by long wing-fingers.

facts.statement: Cimoliopterus possibly fed while flying by dipping its long jaws into water to catch fish with interlocking teeth.
facts.quote: They possibly fed while flying by dipping their long jaws into water and catching fish with their interlocking teeth.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the premaxillary crests of Cimoliopterus were used to stabilize jaws during feeding or served as display structures.
facts.quote: While some have suggested the premaxillary crests were used to stabilise the jaws while submerged in water during feeding, they may have been used as display structures.

facts.statement: A single tooth originally reported in the holotype snout had disappeared by the time it was examined in the 2000s.
facts.quote: It was originally reported to preserve a single tooth in the first right tooth socket (at the front of the snout), but this had disappeared when the holotype was examined in the 2000s.

facts.statement: Richard Owen assigned a long bone catalogued as NHMUK PV 41637 to Pterodactylus cuvieri in 1851, identifying it as a possible phalanx bone of the wing-finger.
facts.quote: The British biologist Richard Owen assigned one long bone to P. cuvieri in 1851 (today catalogued as NHMUK PV 41637) based on its size and the character of its surface, and identified it as a possible phalanx bone of the elongated wing-finger.

facts.statement: Harry Govier Seeley placed Pterodactylus cuvieri in the new genus Ptenodactylus in 1869 in an index of specimens at the Woodwardian Museum.
facts.quote: In 1869, the British palaeontologist Harry Govier Seeley placed P. cuvieri in the new genus "Ptenodactylus" along with other English pterosaurs known mainly from upper jaws, in an index of specimens in the Woodwardian Museum.

facts.statement: Harry Govier Seeley placed the species in the genus Ornithocheirus in 1870 and listed a dentary bone as belonging to O. cuvieri.
facts.quote: In 1870, Seeley placed the species in the genus Ornithocheirus, which he had originally used for other species in his 1869 index, and figured a dentary bone (front bone of the mandible) he listed belonged to O. cuvieri.

facts.statement: Richard Owen assigned the species to the genus Coloborhynchus in 1874.
facts.quote: In 1874, Owen assigned the species to the genus Coloborhynchus.

facts.statement: Franz Nopcsa von Felső-Szilvás criticized Gustav von Arthaber's skull reconstructions in 1924, calling some of them worthless.
facts.quote: In 1924, von Arthaber's interpretations were criticised by the Hungarian palaeontologist Franz Nopcsa von Felső-Szilvás, who found some of the skull reconstructions "worthless".

facts.statement: Peter Wellnhofer noted similarities between the Brazilian pterosaur Tropeognathus and English taxa based on fragmentary snouts in 1987.
facts.quote: In 1987, the German palaeontologist Peter Wellnhofer described the new crested pterosaur Tropeognathus from the Santana Formation of Brazil and noted the similarities between it and other newly described Brazilian taxa such as Anhanguera to English taxa that were based on fragmentary snouts, such as the various species assigned to Ornithocheirus.

facts.statement: Alexander W. Kellner and colleagues established the new genus Aussiedraco based on Australian material previously assigned to Anhanguera ?cuvieri in 2011, stating there was no ground for placing O. cuvieri in Anhanguera.
facts.quote: In 2011, the Brazilian palaeontologist Alexander W. Kellner and colleagues made the Australian material that had been assigned to A. ?cuvieri the basis of a new genus, Aussiedraco, and stated that they saw no ground for placing O. cuvieri in Anhanguera.

facts.statement: In 2013, Brazilian paleontologists Taissa Rodrigues and Alexander Kellner reviewed species previously assigned to the genus Ornithocheirus.
facts.quote: In 2013, the Brazilian palaeontologist Taissa Rodrigues and Kellner reviewed the species that had so far been placed in the genus Ornithocheirus

facts.statement: In 2015, Timothy S. Myers described the specimen found by Brent Dunn as the holotype of the new species Cimoliopterus dunni.
facts.quote: In 2015, the American palaeontologist Timothy S. Myers described the specimen and made it the holotype of the new species Cimoliopterus dunni

facts.statement: The specific name dunni honors the collector Brent Dunn, who died in 2013.
facts.quote: The specific name honours Dunn, who died in 2013.

facts.statement: In 2025, Rubi V. Pêgas assigned the species O. colorhinus to the genus Cimoliopterus.
facts.quote: In 2025, Pêgas assigned O. colorhinus from the Cambridge Greensand to Cimoliopterus as the new combination C. colorhinus

facts.statement: The generic name Cimoliopterus combines the Greek words for chalk and wing.
facts.quote: This generic name combines the Greek words Kimolia (Κιμωλία), which means "chalk", and pteron, (πτερόν) meaning "wing".

facts.statement: The full translation of the genus name is "Cuvier's chalk wing".
facts.quote: In full, the name can be translated as "Cuvier's chalk wing".

facts.statement: The size of Cimoliopterus is difficult to estimate because the available fossils are incomplete.
facts.quote: Because the fossils are incomplete, the size of Cimoliopterus is difficult to estimate.

facts.statement: In 1851, Bowerbank estimated the wingspan of Cimoliopterus cuvieri to be about 16.6 feet.
facts.quote: Bowerbank estimated a wingspan of about 16.6 ft in 1851.

facts.statement: In 2001, Unwin estimated the wingspan of Cimoliopterus cuvieri to be about 3.5 meters based on comparisons with Anhanguera.
facts.quote: In 2001, comparing the C. cuvieri holotype specimen with the more complete Anhanguera, Unwin estimated a wingspan of about 3.5 m.

facts.statement: In 2023, Witton and Michel estimated a wingspan of 4 meters for C. cuvieri, noting the estimate was rough due to poor fossil quality.
facts.quote: Witton and Michel gave a 4 m wingspan for C. cuvieri in 2023, but cautioned it was "rough" due to the poor fossils.

facts.statement: Cimoliopterus dunni was estimated to have a wingspan of about 6 feet, making it mid-sized for a pterosaur.
facts.quote: C. dunni would have been mid-sized for a pterosaur, with a wingspan of about 6 ft, according to a press release accompanying its description.

facts.statement: The holotype snouts of Cimoliopterus species are distinguished from other pterodactyloids by a premaxillary crest that begins further back on the snout.
facts.quote: The holotype snouts of the two Cimoliopterus species share features that distinguish them from other pterodactyloid (or short-tailed) pterosaurs such as a premaxillary crest that begins hindward on the snout

facts.statement: The snout tips of C. cuvieri and C. dunni show only subtle sideways expansion, unlike the spoon-like expansions seen in other toothed pteranodontoids.
facts.quote: The snout tips of C. cuvieri and C. dunni are only expanded subtly from side to side, unlike the "spoon-like" expansions seen in many other toothed pteranodontoids

facts.statement: Much of the Cimoliopterus skeleton was likely pneumatized, filled with air sacs that lightened the body.
facts.quote: Much of the skeleton would have been pneumatised (filled with air sacs that lightened it).

facts.statement: Cimoliopterus had forelimbs proportionally enormous compared to its legs, featuring very long wing-fingers.
facts.quote: The forelimbs were proportionally enormous compared to the legs, with very long wing-fingers.

facts.statement: Cimoliopterus was covered in pycnofibres, hair-like filaments, and possessed extensive wing membranes.
facts.quote: As a pterosaur, Cimoliopterus would have been covered in pycnofibres (hair-like filaments), and had extensive wing-membranes

facts.statement: Rodrigues and Kellner concluded that A. cuvieri differed enough from its relatives to warrant placement in the new monotypic genus Cimoliopterus.
facts.quote: They concluded that A. cuvieri differed enough from its relatives to be placed in a new, monotypic genus; Cimoliopterus.

facts.statement: Rodrigues and Kellner considered P. fittoni, O. brachyrhinus, and O. enchorhynchus too fragmentary to assign to Cimoliopterus, classifying them as nomina dubia.
facts.quote: Rodrigues and Kellner also found that while the species P. fittoni, O. brachyrhinus, and O. enchorhynchus had various features in common with C. cuvieri, and could therefore not be excluded from that genus, they were too fragmentary to be assigned to it definitively and were considered nomina dubia (dubious names).

facts.statement: The holotype of Cimoliopterus cuvieri consists of the front 7 inches of the snout, primarily including the premaxillae and the premaxillary crest.
facts.quote: The holotype of C. cuvieri is composed of the front 7 in of the snout, represented mainly by the premaxillae, including the premaxillary crest.

facts.statement: C. cuvieri has a low snout and a forward-facing first pair of tooth sockets, distinguishing it from Ornithocheirus.
facts.quote: C. cuvieri has a low snout compared to Ornithocheirus and also possesses a forward-facing first pair of tooth sockets, unlike that genus.

facts.statement: C. cuvieri is distinguished from the genus Anhanguera by the lack of an expansion at the front of the snout.
facts.quote: C. cuvieri can be distinguished from the genus Anhanguera because it lacks an expansion at the front of the snout, a feature otherwise present in the family Anhangueridae.

facts.statement: Bowerbank and Owen described and illustrated the teeth found with the C. cuvieri holotype in 1851.
facts.quote: Bowerbank and Owen described and figured the now lost teeth found with the C. cuvieri holotype in 1851.

facts.statement: The teeth of C. cuvieri were composed of compact, hard dentine sheathed by a thin coat of enamel.
facts.quote: The tips were broken off, revealing they were composed of compact, hard dentine, that was sheathed by a thin coat of enamel.

facts.statement: The enamel of C. cuvieri teeth is marked by fine, longitudinal ridges of unequal length with wide intervals.
facts.quote: Fine, longitudinal ridges (or striations) unequal in length, with wide intervals mark the enamel.

facts.statement: Twenty-six tooth sockets are preserved in the C. dunni holotype specimen.
facts.quote: The total number of tooth sockets preserved in the specimen is twenty-six.

facts.statement: C. dunni is distinguished from C. cuvieri by a premaxillary crest that begins at the fourth socket pair and is slightly upwardly curved with a concave front edge.
facts.quote: C. dunni is distinguished by the premaxillary crest beginning at the fourth socket pair, unlike that of C. cuvieri, and the crest is slightly upwards curved, forming a front edge that is concave.

facts.statement: The complete fusion of the crest to the jaw in C. dunni indicates the individual was not a juvenile.
facts.quote: The crest is fused entirely to the jaw, which indicates the individual was not a juvenile.

facts.statement: If symmetrical, the complete premaxillary crest of C. dunni would have measured approximately 15 to 16 cm in length.
facts.quote: If the crest was symmetrical, the complete crest would have had a length of approximately 15 to 16 cm.

facts.statement: The maximum height of the C. dunni crest is 38 mm, located above the ninth and tenth pairs of tooth sockets.
facts.quote: The maximum height of the crest is 38 mm, which is above the ninth and tenth pair of tooth sockets.

facts.statement: The snout tip of C. dunni is blunt.
facts.quote: The tip of the snout in C. dunni is blunt.

facts.statement: The width of the C. dunni snout increases towards the back, reaching a maximum of 1.8 to 1.9 cm at the broken hind edge of the crest.
facts.quote: The width of the snout continues increasing hindward until it reaches a maximum of 1.8 to 1.9 cm at the broken part of the hind edge of the crest.

facts.statement: A narrow palatal ridge less than 1 mm high extends toward the front from the broken rear end of the premaxillary crest in C. dunni.
facts.quote: At less than 1 mm high, a narrow palatal ridge extends towards the front from the broken portion on the rear end of the premaxillary crest.

facts.statement: It is uncertain whether C. colorhinus had a crest because all known specimens are incomplete.
facts.quote: Since all the specimens are incomplete, it is uncertain if this species had a crest.

facts.statement: James Scott Bowerbank described the type species Pterodactylus cuvieri in 1851 from fossils found in a limestone quarry near Maidstone in Kent.
facts.quote: En 1851, James Scott Bowerbank nombró y describió algunos restos hallados en una cantera de caliza en Burham cerca de Maidstone en Kent, como una nueva especie de Pterodactylus: Pterodactylus cuvieri.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen NHMUK PV 39409 was found in the Chalk Formation dating from the Cenomanian to Turonian stages.
facts.quote: El holotipo, NHMUK PV 39409, fue hallado en una capa de la Formación Chalk que data de entre el Cenomaniense al Turoniense.

facts.statement: Taissa Rodrigues and Alexander Wilhelm Armin Kellner established the separate genus Cimoliopterus in 2013.
facts.quote: En 2013, Taissa Rodrigues y Alexander Wilhelm Armin Kellner crearon un género separado: Cimoliopterus.

facts.statement: Cimoliopterus is closely related to Aetodactylus, a pteranodontoid found in Cenomanian strata in Texas.
facts.quote: El análisis filogenético de la descripción de esta especie indica que Cimoliopterus es un pteranodontoideo cercanamente relacionado con Aetodactylus, también hallado en estratos cenomanienses de Texas.

facts.statement: Cimoliopterus lived between 100.5 and 89.8 million years ago during the Cenomanian to Turonian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Cenomanian to Turonian (100.5 to 89.8 million years ago)

facts.statement: The genus name Cimoliopterus is derived from Kimolia, the white limestone of the island of Kimolos, and the Greek word pteron meaning wing.
facts.quote: El nombre de género se deriva de Κιμωλία, Kimolia, la caliza blanca de la isla Kímolos (kimolia significa "caliza" en griego) junto al término griego latinizado πτερόν, pteron, "ala".

facts.statement: Rodrigues and Kellner identified two unique derived traits for Cimoliopterus in 2013: a crest located far forward on the premaxilla at the level of the seventh tooth pair but starting before the nasoantorbital fenestra.
facts.quote: En 2013, Rodrigues y Kellner establecieron dos rasgos únicos derivados o autapomorfias, para Cimoliopterus, que lo diferencian de sus parientes: su cresta se sitúa muy lejos en el premaxilar, al nivel del séptimo par de dientes, pero empieza antes de la fenestra nasoantorbitalis, la gran baertura en el cráneo

facts.statement: Cimoliopterus possesses a unique combination of general traits including a crested snout, a palatal ridge reaching the third tooth pair, an upwardly curved palate, lack of a frontal mandibular expansion, and second and third tooth pairs being equal in size and larger than the fourth pair.
facts.quote: Aparte de esto Cimoliopterus muestra una combinación única de rasgos más generales: el hocico tiene una cresta; el borde en la zona media del paladar en el frente alcanza el nivel del tercer par de dientes; el paladar se curva hacia arriba; carece de una expansión de la mandíbula en el frente; el segundo y tercer par de dientes son igual de grandes y mayores que el cuarto par de dientes

facts.statement: In 1851, Bowerbank estimated the wingspan of P. cuvieri to be nearly 5.04 meters based on extrapolations from P. giganteus fossils, making it the largest known living or extinct flying animal at that time.
facts.quote: Bowerbank, haciendo extrapolaciones a partir de los restos de P. giganteus, estimó que la envergadura de P. cuvieri sería de cerca de 5.04 metros, lo cual lo convierte el animal volador de mayor tamaño vivo o extinto conocido en 1851.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Ornithocheirus brachyrhinus and Pterodactylus fittoni belong to Cimoliopterus cuvieri, as they share characteristics but are too incomplete for definitive referral, leading Rodrigues and Kellner to classify them as nomina dubia.
facts.quote: Ornithocheirus brachyrhinus Seeley 1870 y Pterodactylus fittoni Owen 1859 comparten varias características con C. cuvieri, y por tanto no se puede excluir que sean parte del mismo taxón. Sin embargo, son demasiado incompletos como para ser referidos definitivamente a C. cuvieri, por lo que Rodrigues y Kellner los consideraron nomina dubia.

facts.statement: Rodrigues and Kellner assigned Cimoliopterus to the group Pteranodontoidea with an uncertain position (incertae sedis).
facts.quote: Cimoliopterus fue asignado por Rodrigues y Kellner al grupo Pteranodontoidea, en una posición incierta (incertae sedis).

facts.statement: The discovery of Cimoliopterus dunni extends the genus's distribution to North America, indicating that European and North American pterosaur faunas maintained contact in the mid-Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Este hallazgo extiende la distribución del género a Norteamérica y muestra que las faunas de pterosaurios de Europa y Norteamérica aún mantenían contacto a mediados del Cretácico.
